messages:
anna: Posting from support — customer 'ACME' seeing indexer rejects after embedding model swap. Root error: indexer rejecting batches with \"vector dimension mismatch\". Any quick triage?

jess: @anna can you paste the error payload and which model they switched to? :eyes:

 tom_customer: hey team, here's what our logs show when submitting doc batch to /index:
```
ERROR indexer: failed to insert vectors: invalid vector size: expected=1536 got=1024
batch_id=2024-05-03T15:22:10Z
payload_sample={\"id\":\"doc-9923\",\"embedding_len\":1024}
```
also we started seeing 429s on ingest around same time.

anna: they said they pointed at 'rwd-embed-2' yesterday evening (last night) — iirc that one is a 1024 model. previous was 'rwd-embed-legacy' 1536.

mike: yep confirmed — rwd-embed-2 uses 1024. We rolled it to canary across hosted endpoints at ~2024-05-03T19:00 UTC. We didn't update indexer schema mapping.

sara: so indexer (vecdb) expects 1536 vectors. When it gets 1024 it rejects. The 429s are probably the client retrying while the ingestion worker fails fast.

alex: quick mitigation options:
- rollback routing to rwd-embed-legacy (1536) for that customer
- or add a temporary embedding-to-legacy shim: pad embeddings with zeros to 1536 before indexer
- or trigger a backfill/normalization job to re-embed or upcast stored vectors

jess: customer is asking for fastest fix — rollback will restore service but block cost/latency improvements.

tom_customer: rollback is fine short-term. We want a plan for backfill though; we can't lose the new model improvements.

mike: agree. For backfill we'll need to choose:
- re-run embedding job on source texts with new model (preferred for quality)
- or upcast 1024->1536 by concatenating zeros (cheap but changes semantics)

sara: note: any padding will break similarity scores relative to true 1536 embeddings. If they use cosine similarity, padding zeros reduces magnitude but cosine may still be impacted.

anna: repro steps I asked the customer to run to confirm locally:
```
curl -s -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings\" \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-embed-2\",\"input\":[\"test doc\"]}' | jq .data[0].embedding | wc -l
# should print 1024
```

mike: dev tip — add a server-side dim check in the indexer pipeline before attempting insert. Reject early with a helpful message and a code 422 so clients can handle.

alex: i'm adding a safe-fallback option in the ingestion config so teams can choose 'pad_to_dim' or 'reject_on_dim_mismatch'. i'll PR a config schema change.

sara: ops plan: rollback routing for ACME now, start backfill job template across their 120k docs next — estimate: 6h on our Dedicated pool if batching 256 and concurrency 8. We'll monitor token cost.

jess: documented runbook steps for support:
1) identify affected customer + model id
2) switch routing to previous model if available
3) run quick health check on a 10-doc sample
4) schedule backfill or enable pad_to_dim (with note to customer)
5) follow up with postmortem

deploy-bot: deploy request queued by @alex for 'ingest-config:pad-to-dim' ✅

tom_customer: thanks all. we'll accept rollback for now. can you confirm ETA for backfill kickoff?

sara: starting backfill job in 30m. tagging ops channel. i'll update thread when it completes and share metrics.

mike: follow-up actions for platform team:
- add dim-check unit in CI for model onboarding
- surface model embedding dim in catalog UI and API responses
- add automated notice on model promotion that dims changed

anna: i'll send customer-facing note outlining options and timeline. :thumbsup:

jess: adding a short postmortem ticket and linking to this thread.

sara: status update 35m later: backfill job started, processing avg 900 docs/min, current ETA ~5.9h. no additional errors so far. :white_check_mark:

anna: closing the support escalation after handoff to ops; keeping this thread for the postmortem.
